record.title: OD-characterizability conjecture for projective special linear groups over the binary field
record.statement: Let $L_n(2)$ denote the projective special linear group over the binary field, for an integer $n\geqslant 2$. A finite group is **OD-characterizable** if it is uniquely determined, up to isomorphism, by its order and degree pattern. **OD-characterizability conjecture.** The groups $L_n(2)$ are OD-characterizable for all integers $n\geqslant 2$. This conjecture concerns recognition of these finite simple groups from their order and prime graph degree pattern; the source confirms the claim for $L_{10}(2)$ and $L_{11}(2)$, while the general case remains open in the provided text.
record.source_name: A. R. Moghaddamfar and S. Rahbariyan, “OD-Characterization of Some Linear Groups Over Binary Field and Their Automorphism”, arXiv:1304.7333 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7333

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2013).

record.title: Clifford-type bound for stable coherent systems on quintic surfaces
record.statement:
Let $S\subset\mathbb{P}^3$ be a smooth quintic surface and let $h=c_1(\mathcal{O}_S(1))$. A coherent system on $S$ is a morphism $(\mathcal{O}_S^{\oplus R}\to F)$; let $\mu'$ denote the slope stability function used in the source.

**Clifford-type bound conjecture.** For every $\mu'$-stable coherent system $(\mathcal{O}_S^{\oplus R}\to F)$ with

$$
R=2\operatorname{rank}(F)>0,
$$

one has

$$
\frac{c_1(F)\cdot h}{R}>\frac{5}{8}+\frac{c}{b}=1.3818\cdots.
$$

This conjecture is intended to provide the inequality needed for the double-tilting construction of a Gepner-type stability condition on the corresponding matrix-factorization category. The source does not prove the bound.
record.source_name: Yukinobu Toda, “Gepner point and strong Bogomolov-Gieseker inequality for quintic 3-folds”, arXiv:1305.0345 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.0345

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Genus two G-function vanishing conjecture for ADE Frobenius manifolds
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a Frobenius manifold associated to an ADE singularity or to an extended affine Weyl group of ADE type. Its genus two free energy has a decomposition

$$
\mathcal{F}_2=\sum_{p=1}^{16}c_pQ_p+G^{(2)}(u,u_x,u_{xx}),
$$

where the $Q_p$ are contributions represented by genus zero correlation functions and $G^{(2)}(u,u_x,u_{xx})$ is the genus two $G$-function.

**Genus two G-function vanishing conjecture.** For every such $M$,

$$
G^{(2)}(u,u_x,u_{xx})=0.
$$

The conjecture concerns the vanishing of the non-explicit genus two contribution in the free energy for Frobenius manifolds arising from ADE singularities and extended affine Weyl groups of ADE type. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Yulong Fu, Si-Qi Liu, Youjin Zhang and Chunhui Zhou, “Proof of a Conjecture on the Genus Two Free Energy Associated to the A_n Singularity”, arXiv:1305.1008 (2013).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2012–2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1205.5990](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.5990).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.1008

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Rudolph's popularity conjecture for 132-avoiding patterns
record.statement:
Let $\tau$ and $\mu$ be permutation patterns, and let $A_n(\tau)$ and $A_n(\mu)$ denote their total numbers of occurrences among permutations in $S_n(132)$. Associate to each pattern its binary tree $T(\tau)$ or $T(\mu)$, and let its spine structure be ordered by refinement order. **Rudolph's popularity conjecture.** For all $n$, 
$$
A_n(\tau) \le A_n(\mu)
$$
 if and only if the spine structure of $T(\tau)$ is less than or equal to the spine structure of $T(\mu)$ in refinement order. This conjecture seeks a complete characterization of the popularity order on 132-avoiding permutation patterns; Rudolph had previously proved equality of popularities when the corresponding trees have the same spine structure.
record.source_name: Natalie Aisbett, “A relation on 132-avoiding permutation patterns”, arXiv:1305.5128 (2014).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.5128

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).

record.title: Lehmer's conjecture for the Ramanujan tau coefficients
record.statement:
Let $q=e^{2\pi i z}$, and let

$$
\Delta_k(z)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\tau_k(n)q^n\in S_k^{\operatorname{new}}(\Gamma_0(1))
$$

be a newform, where $k\in\{12,16,18,20,22,26\}$. **Lehmer's conjecture.** For every such $k$ and every positive integer $n$,

$$
\tau_k(n)\neq0.
$$

For $k=12$, this is Lehmer's question about the nonvanishing of the Ramanujan tau function, and the source states that it remains open, as do analogous questions for the other listed newforms.
record.source_name: Jeremy Rouse and Jesse Thorner, “The Explicit Sato-Tate Conjecture and Densities Pertaining to Lehmer-Type Questions”, arXiv:1305.5283 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.5283

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2013). “The Sato-Tate Conjecture describes a distribution that was proven affirmatively by Barnet-Lamb, Geraghty, Harris, and Taylor in : [The Sato-Tate Conjecture] Let $f(z)\in S_k^{\textup{new}}(\Gamma_0(N),\chi)$ be a non-CM newform.”

record.title: The surviving-rate conjecture for square grids
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices, and let $P_n\square P_n$ be the Cartesian product of two such paths. Write $\rho(G)$ for the expected percentage of vertices saved when a fire starts at a uniformly random vertex of the finite graph $G$. **The square-grid surviving-rate conjecture.**

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho(P_n\square P_n)=\frac{5}{8}.
$$

The paper proves matching lower bounds of $5/8+o(1)$ and an upper bound differing by less than $0.0136$, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Tomas Gavenciak, Jan Kratochvil and Pawel Pralat, “Firefighting on square, hexagonal, and triangular grids”, arXiv:1305.7076 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.7076

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2013). “It is natural to conjecture the following but this still remains open.”

record.title: Congruence for 9-regular partitions modulo 12
record.statement:
Let $b_9(n)$ denote the number of $9$-regular partitions of $n$, that is, partitions in which no part divisible by $9$ appears. **The higher-power congruence.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$,

$$
b_9(32k+13)\equiv 0\pmod{12}.
$$

This extends the proved divisibility congruences for $9$-regular partitions modulo $3$ and $6$ to a progression associated with a higher power of $2$; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: William J. Keith, “Congruences for 9-regular partitions modulo 3”, arXiv:1306.0136 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0136

record.title: Hirschhorn–Sellers congruence for overpartitions
record.statement:
Let an **overpartition** of a nonnegative integer be a partition in which the first occurrence of each part may be overlined, and let $\bar{p}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$, with $\bar{p}(0)=1$. For every integer $n\geq 0$, **Hirschhorn–Sellers' conjecture.**

$$
\bar{p}(40n+35)\equiv 0 \pmod {40}.
$$

This is a Ramanujan-type divisibility conjecture for the overpartition function. The conjecture is stated in the source as an open conjecture; the paper proves it using generating functions and modular-form methods.
record.source_name: William Y. C. Chen and Ernest X. W. Xia, “Proof of a Conjecture of Hirschhorn and Sellers on Overpartitions”, arXiv:1307.4155 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.4155

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of July 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The doublet and sextet conjecture for umbral modules
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a Niemeier root system with Coxeter number $m$. A representation is a **doublet** if it is the direct sum of two copies of one representation, and a **sextet** if it is the direct sum of six copies of one representation. **Doublet and sextet conjecture.** The representation $K^X_{r,-D/4m}$ is a doublet if and only if $D\ne0$ and $D\ne-n\lambda^2$ for every integer $\lambda$ and every $n$ listed in the source's discriminant table for $X$. If $X=A_8^3$, then $K^X_{r,-D/4m}$ is a sextet if and only if

$$
D\ne-27\lambda^2
$$

for some integer $\lambda$. The source presents this as a conjecture based on observed multiplicity patterns; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Miranda C. N. Cheng, John F. R. Duncan and Jeffrey A. Harvey, “Umbral Moonshine and the Niemeier Lattices”, arXiv:1307.5793 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.5793

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2013).

record.title: Existence and non-existence conjecture for ${\cal A}\cT_{n,\omega_U}$
record.statement: Let ${\cal A}\cT_{n,\omega_U}$ denote the fusion category associated with the construction considered in the paper, indexed by an integer $n$ and a parameter $\omega_U$. The preceding results show non-existence for $4\leq n\leq 10$ and force $\omega_U=1$ whenever the category exists in the cases studied. **Existence and non-existence conjecture.** The technique used for the preceding uniqueness and non-existence theorems should show that ${\cal A}\cT_{n,\omega_U}$ exists only if $\omega_U=1$ for all $1\leq n<\infty$, and that ${\cal A}\cT_{n,\omega_U}$ does not exist for all $4\leq n<\infty$. This would extend the computed results to all values of $n$, ruling out the construction from $n=4$ onward and leaving only the parameter value $\omega_U=1$ as a possibility.
record.source_name: Masaki Izumi, Scott Morrison and David Penneys, “Fusion categories between C D and C * D”, arXiv:1308.5723 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.5723

record.title: Nonvanishing of the order-five obstruction outside exceptional parameter values
record.statement:
Let $K_{4,36}$ denote the order-five variational-equation entry obtained by transporting the jet along the cycle $\gamma=\gamma_-^{-1}\gamma_+^{-1}\gamma_-\gamma_+$. Let $(\Lambda,\lambda)$ be the parameters of the Friedmann–Robertson–Walker Hamiltonian, and let $n=0,1$ refer to the exceptional cases listed in the source's equation (exc). **Nonvanishing conjecture.**

$$
K_{4,36}\neq 0
$$

for every value of $(\Lambda,\lambda)$ except for $n=0,1$ in (exc). Hence, the order-five variational equations yield the first obstruction to integrability in $H$. The claim is presented as an open problem supported by uniform numerical evidence for $k=5$ and by the preceding non-integrability theorem.
record.source_name: Sergi Simon, “Conditions and evidence for non-integrability in the Friedmann-Robertson-Walker Hamiltonian”, arXiv:1309.2754 (2015).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2754

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2013). “Let us now use the same procedure on an open problem.”

record.title: Conjecture on the number of linear relations in length two
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 4$. Consider the linear relations among the generators of the weight-$k$, length-two component $\operatorname{gr}^{\operatorname{W},\operatorname{L}}_{k,2}\operatorname{q\mathcal{M}\mathcal{Z}}$. **The relation-count conjecture.** For every weight $k\geq 4$, the number of such linear relations equals

$$
\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2}\right\rfloor-1.
$$

The authors verified the claim for $k\leq 20$, where this method produced all observed length-two relations; the assertion is proposed on the basis of that computation.
record.source_name: Henrik Bachmann and Ulf Kuehn, “The algebra of generating functions for multiple divisor sums and applications to multiple zeta values”, arXiv:1309.3920 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.3920

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2013).

record.title: The consecutive-integers prime conjecture between consecutive squares
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Consider $n$ consecutive integers $a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n$ satisfying

$$
n^2<a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n<(n+1)^2.
$$

**Consecutive-integers prime conjecture.** At least one of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ is prime.

This conjecture concerns the existence of primes in intervals between consecutive squares and would imply Legendre's, Brocard's, Andrica's, and Oppermann's conjectures, as well as related prime-gap bounds. The paper reports verification for every $n$ with $1\leq n\leq 1,193,806,023$, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Germán Paz, “On Legendre's, Brocard's, Andrica's, and Oppermann's Conjectures”, arXiv:1310.1323 (2014).

record.title: The bipartite Turán graph conjecture for cycle-maximal triangle-free graphs
record.statement:
Let a **cycle-maximal triangle-free graph** be a triangle-free graph to which no edge can be added without creating a triangle. For a graph on $n$ vertices, let $K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}$ denote the balanced complete bipartite graph. **The bipartite Turán graph conjecture.** The cycle-maximal triangle-free graphs are exactly the bipartite Turán graphs

$$
K_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor, \lceil n/2 \rceil}
$$

for all $n$. The conjecture was verified by exhaustive computer search for $n\leq 13$; it proposes that balanced complete bipartite graphs maximize the number of cycles among cycle-maximal triangle-free graphs.
record.source_name: Stephane Durocher, David S. Gunderson, Pak Ching Li and Matthew Skala, “Cycle-maximal triangle-free graphs”, arXiv:1310.5172 (2014).

record.title: Savage–Visontai equidistribution conjecture for signed multiset permutations
record.statement: Let $s=(1,4,3,8,5,12,\ldots)$, with $s_{2i}=4i$ and $s_{2i-1}=2i-1$ for $i\geq 1$. Let $I_n$ be the set of $s$-inversion sequences of length $n$, and let $P_n$ be the set of signed permutations on the multiset $\{1^2,2^2,\ldots,n^2\}$. **Savage–Visontai conjecture.** For every $n\geq 1$, the descent number over $P_n$ is equidistributed with the ascent number over $I_{2n}$. This conjecture would imply the real-rootedness of the generating function for the descent number over $P_n$; the cited context states that real-rootedness is known for ascent-number generating functions over arbitrary $s$-inversion sequences.
record.source_name: William Y. C. Chen, Alan J. X. Guo, Peter L. Guo, Harry H. Y. Huang and Thomas Y. H. Liu, “s-Inversion Sequences and P-Partitions of Type B”, arXiv:1310.5313 (2013).

record.title: Monotonicity conjecture for the relative Banzhaf power index
record.statement:
Let $n_1,n_2$ be the numbers of players of the two types, and let $Bz_2(a,b,n_1,n_2)$ denote the relative Banzhaf power index of a player of type $2$ in the corresponding complete simple game. **Relative Banzhaf monotonicity conjecture.**

For $b\geq 1$,

$$
Bz_2(a,b,n_1,n_2)-Bz_2(a,b-1,n_1,n_2)>0.
$$

For $a\geq 2$,

$$
Bz_2(a-1,b,n_1,n_2)-Bz_2(a,b,n_1,n_2)\geq 0,
$$

with equality for $b=0$ and a strict inequality otherwise. The conjecture would imply a corollary analogous to the stated ordering result for the relative Banzhaf index; it is supported in the source by verification for all $n\leq 100$.
record.source_name: Josep Freixas and Sascha Kurz, “Enumeration of weighted games with minimum and an analysis of voting power for bipartite complete games with minimum”, arXiv:1310.6113 (2013).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.6113

record.title: Dominance-order conjecture for cuspidal classes of the symmetric group
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be partitions with only odd parts, and let $\mathcal{O}_\lambda$ and $\mathcal{O}_\mu$ be the corresponding cuspidal classes of the symmetric group. The dominance order on partitions is defined by $\mu \trianglelefteq \lambda$ when, for every positive integer $k$, the sum of the first $k$ parts of $\mu$ is at most the sum of the first $k$ parts of $\lambda$. **Dominance-order conjecture.** The classes satisfy

$$
\mathcal{O}_\lambda \leq \mathcal{O}_\mu
$$

if and only if

$$
\mu \trianglelefteq \lambda.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the partial ordering on cuspidal twisted conjugacy classes agrees, under the parametrization by odd-part partitions, with the dominance order. It had been checked by computer for $n\leq 10$ in the source.
record.source_name: Olivier Dudas and Gunter Malle, “Decomposition matrices for low rank unitary groups”, arXiv:1310.7379 (2014).

record.title: The LGL stretching property conjecture
record.statement: Let $[a,b]$ be an interval, let $L=L_{[a,b]}:[a,(a+b)/2]\to[a,b]$ be given by $L(x)=2x-a$, and let $\{{\cal G}^{\mathrm{LGL}}_N\}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ be the family of Legendre–Gauss–Lobatto grids. A family of symmetric grids has property $\mathbf{Str}_{\bar N}$ if, for every $N\leq\bar N$, every interval $I\in\mathcal{P}({\cal G}_N)$ with $I\subset(a,a+(b-a)/4]$, and every $I'\in\mathcal{P}({\cal G}_N)$ such that $L(I)\cap I'\neq\varnothing$, one has $|I'|\leq|L(I)|$. **The LGL stretching property conjecture.** The family $\{{\cal G}^{\mathrm{LGL}}_N\}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ has property $\mathbf{Str}_{\bar N}$ for every $\bar N\in\mathbb{N}$. This is supported by numerical verification through order $\bar N=2000$; the assertion for all orders remains open.
record.source_name: Kolja Brix, Claudio Canuto and Wolfgang Dahmen, “Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto grids and associated nested dyadic grids”, arXiv:1311.0028 (2013).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.0028

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2013).

record.title: The monotonicity conjecture for LGL interval quotients
record.statement: Let $\xi^N_0<\xi^N_1<\cdots<\xi^N_N$ be the LGL points, let $\Delta^N_k=[\xi^N_k,\xi^N_{k+1}]$, and define $q_k^N=|\Delta^N_k|/|\Delta^N_{k-1}|$ for the relevant indices. The family has property $\mathbf{MQ}_{\bar N}$ if $q_k^N\leq q_k^{N+1}$ for $N<\bar N$ and fixed $k$, and $q_k^N\geq q_{k+1}^N$ for $1\leq k\leq\lfloor(N-3)/2\rfloor$ and $N\leq\bar N$. **The LGL quotient monotonicity conjecture.** The LGL grids have property $\mathbf{MQ}_{\bar N}$ for every $\bar N\in\mathbb{N}$. Numerical evidence verifies the property through $\bar N=2000$; its validity for all orders remains open.
record.source_name: Kolja Brix, Claudio Canuto and Wolfgang Dahmen, “Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto grids and associated nested dyadic grids”, arXiv:1311.0028 (2013).

record.title: The extremal-function conjecture for generalized Davenport–Schinzel sequences
record.statement:
Let $t_1,t_2,\dots,t_s$ be integers and let $t=\max(t_1,t_2,\dots,t_s)$. For positive integers $r,k,n$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_r(12^{t_1}3^{t_2}\dots s^{t_{s-1}}(s+1)^{t_s}1,k,n)$ denote the corresponding extremal function. **Extremal-function conjecture.** There exists a constant $C$ depending on $t$ such that, for every $r\geq C$, 
$$
\operatorname{Ex}_r(12^{t_1}3^{t_2}\dots s^{t_{s-1}}(s+1)^{t_s}1,k,n)=rn.
$$
 The conjecture extends the exact-value result established immediately beforehand for the pattern treated in the theorem, predicting the same linear extremal value for this broader family of forbidden sequences. The supplied text gives no resolution beyond presenting it as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Kok Bin Wong and Cheng Yeaw Ku, “A generalization of the extremal function of the Davenport-Schinzel sequences”, arXiv:1311.1594 (2013).

record.title: Caporossi's maximal-energy conjecture for unicyclic graphs
record.statement: Let $P_n$ be a path, $C_n$ a cycle, and let $P_n^6$ be the graph obtained by connecting a vertex of $C_6$ to a terminal vertex of $P_{n-6}$. Among all unicyclic graphs on $n$ vertices, the cycle $C_n$ has maximal energy if $n\leq 7$ and $n=9,10,11,13$ and $15$. **Caporossi's conjecture.** For all other values of $n$, the unicyclic graph with maximal energy is $P_n^6$. The conjecture was stated as a conjecture on maximal energy among unicyclic graphs and is completely solved in the source's subsequent theorem, which adds the exceptional case $n=4$, where $P_4^3$ is maximal.
record.source_name: Xueliang Li, Yongtang Shi, Meiqin Wei and Jing Li, “On a conjecture about tricyclic graphs with maximal energy”, arXiv:1312.0204 (2014).

record.title: Cooper's one-term supercongruences for the sporadic sequences s_7 and s_{18}
record.statement:
Let

$$
s_7(n)=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom{n}{k}^2\binom{n+k}{k}\binom{2k}{n}
$$

and

$$
s_{18}(n)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}(-1)^k\binom{n}{k}\binom{2k}{k}\binom{2(n-k)}{n-k}\left[\binom{2n-3k-1}{n}+\binom{2n-3k}{n}\right],
$$

with $s_{18}(0)=1$. **Cooper's conjecture.** For every prime $p\geqslant3$,

$$
s_7(mp)\equiv s_7(m)\pmod{p^3},
$$

and, for every prime $p$,

$$
s_{18}(mp)\equiv s_{18}(m)\pmod{p^2}.
$$

These congruences are sporadic-sequence analogues of known congruences for Apéry numbers. The paper proves the $s_7$ congruence for $p\geqslant5$ and the $s_{18}$ congruence for all primes; the $s_7$ case for $p=3$ remains open.
record.source_name: Robert Osburn, Brundaban Sahu and Armin Straub, “Supercongruences for sporadic sequences”, arXiv:1312.2195 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.2195

record.title: Knieper's rigidity conjecture for complete Riemannian planes
record.statement: Let $(\mathbb{R}^2,g)$ be a complete Riemannian plane. For a geodesic $\gamma$, say that a geodesic through a point $x\notin\gamma$ is disjoint from $\gamma$ if it does not intersect $\gamma$. **Knieper's conjecture.** If for every geodesic $\gamma$ and every point $x$ outside $\gamma$ there exists a unique geodesic through $x$ that does not intersect $\gamma$, then $g$ is flat. This is a rigidity conjecture in differential geometry, attributed to G. Knieper and stated in 1991. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Xiaojun Cui and Jian cheng, “Busemann functions and barrier functions”, arXiv:1312.4119 (2013).

record.title: Parameter identification conjecture for high-genus triangulation limits
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}_{n,g}$ be the set of rooted triangulations of genus $g$ with $n$ vertices, and let $T_{n,g}$ be uniformly distributed in $\mathcal{T}_{n,g}$. For $\kappa\in(0,\frac{2}{27}]$, define

$$
f(\kappa)=E\left[\left(\operatorname{degree\ of\ the\ origin\ in\ }\mathbf{T}_{\kappa}\right)^{-1}\right].
$$

For $\theta\geq0$, let $\kappa\in(0,\frac{2}{27}]$ satisfy $f(\kappa)=(6(1+2\theta))^{-1}$. **Parameter identification conjecture.**

$$
T_{n,[\theta n]}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{(d)}\mathbf{T}_{\kappa}.
$$

This sharpens the introductory conjecture by matching the finite and infinite models through the inverse degree of the root; the required strict monotonicity and the resulting convergence are not proved in the paper.
record.source_name: Nicolas Curien, “Planar stochastic hyperbolic infinite triangulations”, arXiv:1401.3297 (2014).

record.title: Logarithmic lower-bound conjecture for complete interpolating sequences
record.statement:
Let $\{t_k\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\subset\mathbb{R}$ be an ordered complete interpolating sequence for $\mathcal{PW}_{\pi}^{2}$. **Logarithmic lower-bound conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $C_{12}$ such that

$$
\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\left|\sum_{k=-N}^{N}e^{\mathrm{i}\omega t_k}\widehat{\phi_k}(\omega_1)\right|\,d\omega_1\geq C_{12}\log(N)
$$

for all $\omega\in[-\pi,\pi]$ and all $N\in\mathbb{N}$.
The conjecture is presented as a possible explanation for pointwise-sampling divergence, while the supplied text gives no resolution evidence; it therefore remains open in the database.
record.source_name: Holger Boche and Ullrich J. Mönich, “Signal and System Approximation from General Measurements”, arXiv:1402.1092 (2014).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.1092

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2014). “Conjecture will be proved in Section .”

record.title: The Katz–Klemm–Vafa product formula for BPS counts of K3 surfaces
record.statement:
Let $r_{g,h}$ denote the BPS count associated to a class $\beta$ on a K3 surface whose norm square satisfies

$$
\langle\beta,\beta\rangle=2h-2.
$$

Let $q$ and $y$ be formal variables. **Katz–Klemm–Vafa product formula.** The BPS counts $r_{g,h}$ are uniquely determined by

$$
\sum_{g\geq 0} \sum_{h\geq 0} (-1)^g r_{g,h}(y^{\frac{1}{2}} - y^{-\frac{1}{2}})^{2g}q^h = \prod_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(1-q^n)^{20} (1-yq^n)^2 (1-y^{-1}q^n)^2}.
$$

This formula is the generating-series form of the Katz–Klemm–Vafa prediction and packages the BPS counts for all genera and arithmetic genera. It follows from the preceding conjectural independence from divisibility and is the central product formula for K3 BPS invariants.
record.source_name: R. Pandharipande and R. P. Thomas, “The Katz-Klemm-Vafa conjecture for K3 surfaces”, arXiv:1404.6698 (2017).
record.references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2007–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1103.4230](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4230), [arXiv:0808.0253](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0253), [arXiv:0705.1653](https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.1653).

record.title: Mahler's volume product conjecture
record.statement:
Let $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ be an $n$-dimensional normed space, let $(X^*,\|\cdot\|^*)$ be its dual, and let $B$ and $B^{\circ}$ be the unit balls of $X$ and $X^*$, respectively. Write $\nu(X)$ for the Liouville volume of $B\times B^{\circ}\subset X\times X^*$, also called the Mahler volume or volume product. **Mahler's volume product conjecture.** For every $n$-dimensional normed space $X$,

$$
\nu(X)\geq\frac{4^n}{n!}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the sharp lower bound for the volume product of centrally symmetric convex bodies, with equality attained by the hypercube and, non-uniquely in the broad formulation, its relevant affine counterparts. It was conjectured by Mahler in 1939 and remains an open problem in convex geometry.
record.source_name: Yaron Ostrover, “When symplectic topology meets Banach space geometry”, arXiv:1404.6954 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.6954

record.title: Guo's positive-base Franel-number congruence family
record.statement:
Let the **Franel numbers** be $f_n=\displaystyle\sum_{j=0}^n {n\choose j}^3$. **Guo's conjecture.** For every positive integer $n>1$ and every

$$
(a,b,c)\in\{(9,4,5),(5,2,16),(9,2,50),(5,1,96),(6,1,320),(90,13,896),(102,11,10400)\},
$$

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(ak+b)c^{n-k-1}{2k\choose k}f_k\equiv0\pmod{n{2n\choose n}}.
$$

The authors report verification for $n$ up to $500$, but no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Victor J. W. Guo, “Proof of a supercongruence conjectured by Z.-H. Sun”, arXiv:1404.6978 (2014).

record.title: The regularity conjecture for $H(I,I+2)$
record.statement:
Let $H(I,J)$ be the least positive integer $n$ such that there exist $I$ disjoint Golomb rulers, each a $J$-subset of $\\{1,2,\ldots,n\\}$. **Regularity conjecture.** For every integer $I\geq8$,

$$
H(I,I+2)=I(I+2).
$$

Thus the conjecture predicts regular disjoint Golomb rulers in this parameter range. The paper reports that the assertion has been confirmed computationally for $I\in\\{8,\ldots,150\\}$, but treats the unrestricted statement as conjectural.
record.source_name: Xiu Baoxin, Changjun Fan and Meilian Liang, “On Disjoint Golomb Rulers”, arXiv:1405.4535 (2014).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.4535

record.title: Baker and Rumely's tau lower bound conjecture for metrized graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a metrized graph, let $\ell(\Gamma)=\int_{\Gamma} dx$ be its total length, and consider metrized graphs with $\ell(\Gamma)\neq 0$. **Baker and Rumely's tau lower bound conjecture.**

$$
\text{inf}_{\Gamma}\frac{\tau(\Gamma)}{\ell(\Gamma)}>0,
$$

where the infimum is taken over all metrized graphs $\Gamma$ with nonzero total length. The conjecture asserts the existence of a universal positive lower bound for the tau constant normalized by total length. The paper states a refinement asserting the explicit bound $\tau(\Gamma)>\frac{1}{108}\ell(\Gamma)$ for every metrized graph; the abstract describes $\frac{1}{108}$ as the conjectural lower bound, while the general conjecture is not presented as resolved.
record.source_name: Zubeyir Cinkir, “Families of Metrized Graphs With Small Tau Constants”, arXiv:1405.7005 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7005

record.title: Conjecture on exponential sums associated with Mordell curves
record.statement:
For integers $D$ and $l>0$, define

$$
S(D;3l)=\sum_{\substack{x\pmod{3l}\\4x^2\equiv D\pmod{3l}}}e\left(\frac{4x^3-3Dx}{27l^2}\right),
$$

and, for $Y\geq1$, define

$$
F(D;Y)=\sum_{l\leq Y}\frac{S(D;3l)}{\sqrt l}.
$$

**Exponential-sum conjecture.** If $D$ is not a square, then, uniformly for $D\ll Y^{1+\varepsilon}$,

$$
F(D;Y)\ll Y^{\varepsilon}.
$$

Moreover,

$$
F(0;Y)=3Y^{1/2}+O\left(Y^{5/18+\varepsilon}\right).
$$

These estimates describe the cancellation expected in the nonsquare case and the more precise main term for $D=0$; they are motivated by theoretical and computational evidence and are used to analyze the sum $T_S”(N,X)$.
record.source_name: Matthew P. Young, “The number of solutions to Mordell's equations in constrained ranges”, arXiv:1405.7022 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1405.7022

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2014).

record.title: The characteristically simple Beauville group conjecture
record.statement: A **characteristically simple group** is a finite group isomorphic to $H^k$, where $H$ is finite simple and $k$ is a positive integer. **The characteristically simple Beauville group conjecture.** For every finite characteristically simple group $G$, $G$ is Beauville if and only if $G$ is 2-generated and is not isomorphic to the alternating group $A_5$. The source reports verification for several families and computationally for all such groups of order at most $10^{30}$, while leaving the general statement unresolved.
record.source_name: Ben Fairbairn, “Recent work on Beauville surfaces, structures and groups”, arXiv:1405.7547 (2014).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2014). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1304.5444](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.5444).

record.title: The cube-full Catalan-type equation conjecture
record.statement:
For positive integers $A$ and $B$, call $AB$ **cube-full** when every prime divisor of $AB$ occurs to exponent at least $3$. **The cube-full Catalan-type equation conjecture.** Let $r\geq0$ be an integer. The Diophantine equation

$$
\begin{cases}
A-B=2^r,\\
AB\text{ is cube-full},
\end{cases}
$$

has no solutions for $r=0$, and has the unique solution $(A,B)=(2^{r+1},2^r)$ for $r\geq1$. The source reports computational verification up to $B<A<10^6$, while the assertion for all $r$ remains open.
record.source_name: Tianxin Cai, Yong Zhang and Zhongyan Shen, “Figurate primes and Hilbert's 8th problem”, arXiv:1406.5661 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.5661

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2014).

record.title: The prime-gap cube-full equation conjecture
record.statement:
For positive integers $A$ and $B$, call $AB$ **cube-full** when every prime divisor of $AB$ occurs to exponent at least $3$. **The prime-gap cube-full equation conjecture.** There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that the Diophantine equation

$$
\begin{cases}
A-B=p,\\
AB\text{ is cube-full},
\end{cases}
$$

has no solutions; moreover, the least such prime is $29$. The source states this as a conjecture supported by computation, and no proof of either assertion is given.
record.source_name: Tianxin Cai, Yong Zhang and Zhongyan Shen, “Figurate primes and Hilbert's 8th problem”, arXiv:1406.5661 (2014).

record.title: Kühn, Lapinskas, Osthus, and Patel's linear connectivity conjecture for tournaments
record.statement: A **tournament** is a directed graph with exactly one directed edge between any two distinct vertices. A tournament is **strongly $r$-connected** if deleting fewer than $r$ vertices leaves a strongly connected directed graph. It is **$k$-linked** if, for every two disjoint sets of vertices $\{x_1,\dots,x_k\}$ and $\{y_1,\dots,y_k\}$, there are vertex-disjoint directed paths $P_1,\dots,P_k$ such that $P_i$ goes from $x_i$ to $y_i$. **Kühn, Lapinskas, Osthus, and Patel's conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that every strongly $Ck$-connected tournament is $k$-linked. The conjecture proposes that the known $10^4k\log k$ connectivity bound can be reduced to a linear bound in $k$, beyond the reach of the sorting-network method described in the surrounding discussion.
record.source_name: Alexey Pokrovskiy, “Highly linked tournaments”, arXiv:1406.7552 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.7552

record.title: The twelve-neighbor common-neighbor conjecture for close-packed configurations
record.statement:
Let $Z\subset{\mathbb{R}}^3$ satisfy $|z'-z|\geq 1$ for all $\\{z,z'\\}\subset Z$. For each $z\in Z$, define its nearest-neighbor set by

$$
N(z):=\left\\{z'\in Z:|z'-z|=1\right\\}.
$$

**Common-neighbor conjecture.** If $z,z'\in Z$ satisfy $\\#N(z)=\\#N(z')=12$ and $z\in N(z')$, then

$$
\\#(N(z)\cap N(z'))\geq 4.
$$

This remains an open problem and could provide a route to eliminate the necessity of the three-body potential $V_3$ in the analysis of face-centered cubic crystallization.
record.source_name: Lisa Flatley and Florian Theil, “Face-centered cubic crystallization of atomistic configurations”, arXiv:1407.0692 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.0692

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2014). “Although this remains an open problem, the following conjecture provides a possible route to eliminate the necessity of $V_3.$”

record.title: End-monochromaticity conjecture for selected Rig quandles
record.statement:
A knot $K$ is **end monochromatic with a quandle $X$** when the colors induced at the two endpoints of a $1$-tangle representative of $K$ agree for every coloring by $X$. Let $X$ be one of the following Rig quandles:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&Q(12,1), && Q(20,3), && Q(24,3), && Q(24,4), && Q(24,5),\\
&Q(24,6), && Q(24,14), && Q(24,16), && Q(24,17), && Q(30,1),\\
&Q(30,16), && Q(32,5), && Q(32,6), && Q(32,7), && Q(32,8).
\end{aligned}
$$

**End-monochromaticity conjecture.** Every knot $K$ is end monochromatic with $X$.

The claim generalizes computations showing end monochromaticity for all knots through nine crossings for these quandles. It is used to control colorings of connected sums and to recover information from quandle cocycle invariants; the source gives no proof for all knots.
record.source_name: W. Edwin Clark, M. Saito and L. Vendramin, “Quandle coloring and cocycle invariants of composite knots and abelian extensions”, arXiv:1407.5803 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: Cocycle-invariant support conjecture for the Rig quandle Q(12,5)
record.statement:
Let $X=Q(12,5)$, let $A=\mathbb{Z}_4$, and let $\phi:X\times X\rightarrow A$ be the generating $2$-cocycle chosen in the source's example. For a knot $K$, let $\Phi_\phi(K)$ denote its quandle cocycle invariant, viewed in the group ring $\mathbb{Z}[A]$ and written using a generator $u$ of $A$. **Q(12,5) cocycle-invariant conjecture.** For every knot $K$,

$$
\Phi_\phi(K)=a+bu^2,
$$

where $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$. Computations through eight crossings show this restricted support and motivate the conjecture; the source does not establish it for all knots.
record.source_name: W. Edwin Clark, M. Saito and L. Vendramin, “Quandle coloring and cocycle invariants of composite knots and abelian extensions”, arXiv:1407.5803 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2014).

record.title: Cocycle-invariant support conjecture for the Rig quandle Q(12,10)
record.statement:
Let $X=Q(12,10)$, let $A=\mathbb{Z}_6$, and let $\phi:X\times X\rightarrow A$ be the generating $2$-cocycle chosen in the source's example. For each knot $K$, write its quandle cocycle invariant in $\mathbb{Z}[A]$ as

$$
\Phi_\phi(K)=a+bu+cu^2+du^3+eu^4+fu^5,
$$

where $a,b,c,d,e,f\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $u$ represents a generator of $A$. **Q(12,10) cocycle-invariant conjecture.** For every knot $K$, the coefficients of $u$ and $u^5$ vanish:

$$
b=f=0.
$$

Computations through eight crossings show terms with exponents $2$, $3$ and $4$, but no terms with exponents $1$ or $5$. The conjecture asserts that these latter terms never occur.
record.source_name: W. Edwin Clark, M. Saito and L. Vendramin, “Quandle coloring and cocycle invariants of composite knots and abelian extensions”, arXiv:1407.5803 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.5803

record.title: Prime-graph equality conjecture for intransitive subgroups of alternating groups
record.statement:
Let $G=A_n$ and $H=(S_k\times S_{n-k})\cap G$, where $1<k<n$ and $p\leqslant k$ for every prime number $p\leqslant n$. **Prime-graph equality conjecture.** If $n\geqslant 12$, then

$$
\Gamma(G)=\Gamma(H)
$$

if and only if $n$ is odd, $k=n-1$, and $n-4$ is composite. This concerns the unresolved classification of when an alternating group and an associated intransitive maximal subgroup have the same prime graph; the paper notes that the problem is connected with difficult additive questions about representations of integers as sums of distinct primes.
record.source_name: Timothy C. Burness and Elisa Covato, “On the prime graph of simple groups”, arXiv:1407.8128 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.8128

record.title: The determinant inequality conjecture for configurations of points
record.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the configuration space under consideration, and let $D(\boldsymbol{x})$ denote the associated determinant for $\boldsymbol{x}\in C_n$. **Determinant inequality conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 2$ and every $\boldsymbol{x}\in C_n$, one has

$$
D(\boldsymbol{x})\geq 1.
$$
 This is presented as a stronger conjecture, analogous to Conjecture 2 of Atiyah--Sutcliffe (2002), and it implies the linear independence conjecture. The inequality is verified in the paper for $n=2$, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Joseph Malkoun, “Configurations of Points and the Symplectic Berry-Robbins Problem”, arXiv:1407.8291 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.8291

record.title: The HWM convergent calculation conjecture for Champernowne's constant
record.statement:
Let $C_b$ be Champernowne's constant in base $b$, let $X\geq 0$, and let the $X$th HWM convergent be denoted by the notation used in the source. The integer sequence used to form $C_b$ contains the integers in base-$b$ order.

**HWM convergent calculation conjecture.** The HWM convergent calculates $C_b$ correctly until the integer $T_b(X+1)-2$ is reached, and calculates that integer as $T_b(X+1)-1$ instead.

This is the first conjecture in the paper's extension of the authors' earlier base-$10$ conjectures to arbitrary bases. The stated base-$2$, base-$3$, and base-$4$ exceptions are part of the surrounding discussion, but the parser supplied no resolution evidence.
record.source_name: John K. Sikora, “Analysis of the High Water Mark Convergents of Champernowne's Constant in Various Bases”, arXiv:1408.0261 (2014).

record.title: Correction-factor conjecture for the 2-truncated hook-length formula
record.statement:
Let $[...]$ range over partitions of $n$, let $h_{ij}$ be the hook length of $(i,j)$, and let $[...]$ denote the number of parts of $[...]$ equal to zero as defined in the paper. The 2-truncated hook-length expression is

$$
\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\prod_{\substack{h_{ij}\in\lambda\\h_{ij}=1,2}}\left(1-\frac{b}{h_{ij}^2}\right).
$$

**2-truncation correction conjecture.** For every $n$, its constant, $b$, and $b^2$ coefficients agree with those of

$$
\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\left[\lambda_4\frac{b^2-b^3}{16}+(1-b)^{\ell_0(\lambda)}\prod_{\lambda_j>1}\left(1-\frac{b}{2}\right)\right].
$$

This is reported as a numerical observation intended to identify a correction factor for the unmodified 2-truncation; the source gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: Stability conjecture for half-integer disclination lines
record.statement: Consider disclination lines in the Landau–de Gennes theory, including $7k/2$-disclination lines and the $71/2$-disclination line. **Half-integer disclination-line stability conjecture.** Among all the disclination lines, the $71/2$-disclination line is the most stable. The source notes that this is provable in a special two-dimensional disk setting and proposes that it is generally true for all tensor models of liquid crystals, so the general statement remains open.

record.title: Deflatability conjecture for parallel alternations
record.statement:
Let $pi$ be a **parallel alternation**, meaning a permutation whose entries alternate between two monotone subsequences, with $|pi|\geq 6$. For a permutation $pi$, let $\operatorname{Av}(pi)$ denote the class of permutations avoiding $pi$.

**Deflatability conjecture.** The class $\operatorname{Av}(pi)$ is deflatable.

This conjecture is motivated by explicit deflatability witnesses for several parallel alternations, including $246135$ and longer examples. The general assertion for all parallel alternations of length at least six remains open in the supplied source.
record.source_name: M. H. Albert, M. D. Atkinson, Cheyne Homberger and Jay Pantone, “Deflatability of Permutation Classes”, arXiv:1409.5296 (2014).

record.title: Young graph isomorphism conjecture for the $Y(11,7)$ family
record.statement:
Let $Y(g,k)$ denote the Young graph associated with the base $g$ and multiplier $k$. **$Y(11,7)$ family conjecture.** For all $n\ge 0$, the Young graphs

$$
Y(2(n+2)(n+3)-1, 2(n+2)^2-1),\quad Y(23+20n, 13+12n),\quad Y(23+15n, 17+10n),
$$

$$
Y(26+12n, 10+4n),\quad\text{and}\quad Y(11+6n, 7+3n)
$$

are all isomorphic to $Y(11,7)$. These experimentally observed isomorphisms are part of the paper's computational study of equivalence classes of Young graphs; no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: L. H. Kendrick, “Young Graphs: 1089 et al”, arXiv:1410.0106 (2015).

record.title: Class-number-one conjecture for the first layers of cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions
record.statement: For every prime $p$, let $\mathbb{B}_{p,1}$ be the first layer of the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$. **First-layer class-number conjecture.** For every prime $p$, the class number of $\mathbb{B}_{p,1}$ is $1$. The paper proves or conditionally verifies several initial cases and combines sieve estimates with Cohen–Lenstra heuristics to obtain a probability estimate of at least $75\%$. No proof for all primes is known.
record.source_name: John C. Miller, “Class numbers in cyclotomic Z_p-extensions”, arXiv:1410.2921 (2015).

record.title: Chung's Paley discrepancy conjecture
record.statement:
For primes $p\equiv1\bmod4$, let $\chi$ be the Legendre symbol modulo $p$. Define $\operatorname{PaleyDiscrepancy}[\alpha,\beta]$ to mean that, for every sufficiently large $p$,

$$
\left|\sum_{a,b\in S}\chi(a-b)\right|<|S|^{2-\beta}
$$

for every $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p$ with $|S|>p^\alpha$. **Chung's conjecture.** For each $\alpha>0$, there exists $\beta=\beta(\alpha)>0$ such that $\operatorname{PaleyDiscrepancy}[\alpha,\beta]$. This folklore conjecture appeared as Conjecture 2.2 in Chung (1994), with a proof for $\alpha>1/2$ given there, and has also been used in constructing a pseudorandom number generator. The source does not state a complete resolution for arbitrary $\alpha>0$.
record.source_name: Afonso S. Bandeira, Dustin G. Mixon and Joel Moreira, “A conditional construction of restricted isometries”, arXiv:1410.6457 (2014).

record.title: Bounded-roots conjecture for peak polynomials
record.statement:
Let $S$ be an admissible peak set, let $m=\max(S)$, and let $p_S(z)$ be its peak polynomial. A complex root is a number $z\in\mathbb C$ such that $p_S(z)=0$.

**Bounded-roots conjecture.** Every complex root of $p_S(z)$ lies in

$$
\{z\in\mathbb C: |z|\le m\text{ and }\operatorname{Re}(z)\ge -3\}.
$$

The conjecture is stronger than the positivity conjecture above and is presented as a proposed explanation for positivity of the binomial-basis coefficients. The paper reports experimental verification for all admissible peak sets with $\max(S)\le 15$, but does not prove the conjecture in general.
record.source_name: Sara Billey, Matthew Fahrbach and Alan Talmage, “Coefficients and roots of peak polynomials”, arXiv:1410.8506 (2016).

record.title: Conjecture on the Stanley depth of cyclic graph edge ideals
record.statement:
Let $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring, and let $J_n$ denote the ideal associated with the cyclic graph on $n$ vertices as in the paper. The **Stanley depth conjecture.** For all $n\geq 10$ satisfying $n\equiv 1\pmod{3}$,

$$
\operatorname{sdepth}(S/J_n)=\left\lceil\frac{n}{3}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture concerns the remaining congruence class in the authors' study of the Stanley depth of quotients by ideals associated with line and cyclic graphs; the stated examples support the formula, but the claim is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Mircea Cimpoeas, “On the Stanley depth of edge ideals of line and cyclic graphs”, arXiv:1411.0624 (2015).
